title: Midyear Bridge Plan: OKRs, Exec Sync, Town Outline
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Fast, practical plan to bridge between Q2 and Q3: align leadership, preview updated OKRs, and run a single 60-75 minute midyear town to reset priorities and reduce cross-team churn.
- This doc is a working runbook: agenda, draft OKRs, comm plan, rehearsal checklist, and outstanding decisions.

High-level goals for the session (why we're doing it):
1) Re-anchor company on production priorities: reliability, cost efficiency, and private deployments.
2) Surface measurable OKR changes for next quarter and capture team commitments.
3) Preserve PLG momentum while clarifying enterprise motion handoffs.

Target audience:
- All employees (town), plus an exec-only sync 45m prior with PM/engineering leads invited.

Date proposals (TBD):
- Exec-only dry run: 2025-07-07 10:00-10:45 PT
- Company town: 2025-07-08 13:00-14:15 PT (60-75m)
  - note: consider APAC-friendly repeat or recording + live Q+A window at 08:30 PT next day.

Draft agenda (60-75m town):
- 00:00-00:05: Host welcome, logistics, slate for questions (Priya)
- 00:05-00:20: State of the Product (Maya) — short metrics-driven snapshot: latency, cost/unit, Dedicated backfill, Private pipeline status
  - Slide ask: 3 charts (latency P50/P95 trend, per-token cost trend, adoption by tier).
- 00:20-00:35: Customer stories & impact (CS + Solutions; Zoe) — 2 rapid vignettes: enterprise pilot + PLG success
- 00:35-00:50: OKR preview & ask (Ethan) — present proposed company-level OKRs, highlight changes vs current, call out key tradeoffs
- 00:50-01:05: Roadmap highlights & risk mitigation (Engineering leads panel) — focus on Dedicated SLA work, Private deploys, and Optimize enhancements
- 01:05-01:15: Live Q&A moderated by Daniel — combine Slack/AirTable questions; answer live top 6
- 01:15-01:20: Close, next steps, follow-ups and how teams sign up for OKR workshops

OKR draft (company-level candidates) — initial sketch for discussion:
- OKR 1: Make inference predictable and cost-efficient for customers
  - KR1.1: Reduce average per-token hosting cost by 18% QoQ (baseline May 2025)
  - KR1.2: Achieve P95 latency <= 220ms for Hosted API standard tier under 95th perc throughput
  - KR1.3: Ship intelligent batching and cache auto-tuner to 3 pilot customers

- OKR 2: Enterprise readiness and private offering expansion
  - KR2.1: Onboard 6 new Dedicated customers with SLA contracts signed
  - KR2.2: Complete Private VPC automation runbook and 2 successful on-prem proofs
  - KR2.3: Reduce time-to-deploy Private by 40% (internal baseline)

- OKR 3: Developer experience and PLG momentum
  - KR3.1: Increase active developer integrations by 25% (API signups -> 30-day MAU funnel metric)
  - KR3.2: Launch 4 new quickstarts + 3 reference apps showing cost/latency tradeoffs
  - KR3.3: Hold monthly community evals to validate model quality regressions with automated alerts

Guidance for team-level cascade:
- Week 1 after town: product hosts 60m OKR workshop invite for leads to slot team KRs. Expect 3-week refinement window.
- Use template: "KR: metric, owner, baseline, target, monitor (dashboard link), related tickets".

Comms plan (pre/post town):
- Pre-comms (2 weeks out): executive note + teaser email from CEO; internal blog post w/ one-pager snapshot and easy FAQ. Draft owner: Priya + comms (Daniel to review).
- Town invite + RSVP: calendar + RSVP form (RSVP owner: Zoe). Collect 3 top questions on RSVP.
- Post-comms: publish slides + recording within 24 hours; follow-up town notes and OKR templates in Confluence; track comments in #allhands-ops-thread.

Slide deck outline (internal deck branch: github referenced above):
- Title slide + TL;DR (1 slide)
- Metrics snapshot (3 slides)
- Customer vignettes (2 slides)
- Company-level OKRs (2 slides)
- Roadmap & risk mitigation (3 slides)
- How teams cascade (1 slide)
- FAQ + next steps (1 slide)

Rehearsal & logistics checklist (owners):
- Exec dry run one week prior (Ethan lead) — run full deck, 40m rehearsed + 5m buffer
- AV check (video & livestream) 30m prior (Ops)
- Live Q&A queue: set up AirTable and Slack bridge (Daniel)
- Accessibility: real-time captions + recording (Zoe)
- Feedback capture: one-click pulse survey 24h after (comm)

Open questions / decisions needed before finalizing OKRs:
- Q: What is the exact baseline for per-token cost? Ops/fin to confirm and publish by 2025-06-15. (Action: Daniel -> Fin: ask for per-model cost buckets)
- Q: Do we commit to a single company-level SLA promise for Dedicated in messaging? Legal + Sales to advise. (Action: Priya schedule meeting with Legal)
- Q: Should we run a separate APAC-friendly town or rely on recording + asynchronous Q+A? (Action: Maya to assess regional preference via quick poll)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Metrics variance week before town undermines messaging. Mitigation: freeze snapshot week prior and append errata slide if needed.
- Risk: Overloading teams with immediate KR asks. Mitigation: require 2-week buffer between town and team OKR workshops.

Follow-ups and owners (first pass):
- Finalize company-level OKRs: Ethan (deadline 2025-06-20)
- Baseline cost & latency numbers: Daniel + Finance (deadline 2025-06-15)
- Draft slides and script: Maya + Engineering leads (draft 2025-06-25)
- RSVP form + comms cadence: Zoe (by 2025-06-18)

Notes to self / working fragments (informal):
- Keep exec updates tight — 1 min per slide for leadership section.
- Consider live polling about tradeoff preferences (cost vs latency) — maybe Slido or Loomio?
- Alt plan: if major incident on week of town, shift to recorded format and small live panel for questions.

Linked references and inbox items to resolve:
- Confluence stub: COMPANY/Midyear-Readout-2025 (needs table of contents)
- Jira: INFRA-982 (Dedicated autoscaling work) and PRD-214 (Private automated install)
- Slack thread: #allhands-ops-thread (open for feedback)

Revision history:
- 2025-06-02: initial outline (Priya)
- 2025-06-05: added draft OKRs and agenda (Ethan)
- 2025-06-10: updated rehearsal schedule + owners (Maya)
